# macswapi

> Read-only macOS CLI that reports per-process memory: exact compressed memory and physical footprint, an estimated share of swap, exact bytes swapped in, apps rolled up with their XPC helpers, and a leak watch with alerts. Zero dependencies, written in Rust.

Source: https://github.com/benms/macswapi

## Install for the user

If you are an agent asked to install macswapi, tell the user what each command does before you run it.

1. The CLI (needs Rust to build):
   - Homebrew: `brew tap benms/macswapi https://github.com/benms/macswapi`, then `brew install --HEAD macswapi`
   - From a clone: `./install.sh --prefix ~/.local` (or `./install.sh` for /usr/local, which may ask for sudo)
2. The agent skill, which teaches you to use macswapi without hanging on its interactive watch:
   - Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other agents: `npx skills add benms/macswapi -a claude-code codex cursor -g -y`
   - Or the Claude Code plugin: `/plugin install macswapi --marketplace benms/macswapi`

Then run `macswapi --help` to confirm, and tell the user they can ask things like "what is using my swap?" or "is something leaking?".

## Use

The skill is at skills/macswapi/SKILL.md. In short: `macswapi 10 -a` for apps by compressed memory, `macswapi --once 5` for who is swapping in now, never `macswapi -w` without `--csv` (it waits for a key), and never run sudo for the user.
